Every PMM should be able to complete this sentence without hesitation. If you can’t, your GTM is guessing—not strategizing:

"For [target user], [product] is the [category] that [key benefit] because [reason to believe]."

Most teams skip this step entirely. They jump straight to copy, channels, and ad campaigns...

Then they wonder why nothing lands.

Why? Because there was never a clear position to communicate in the first place.

A few reminders for your next launch:

- Positioning isn't a tagline. It’s the internal filter every single marketing decision passes through.

- If it's confusing internally, it will be completely invisible externally.

 - Strategy precedes execution. Always.

If you're in a PMM role (or aiming for one), spend the entire day nailing this single framework before you write a line of copy.

It will save you months of wasted budget and misaligned messaging.

How does your team define positioning before a launch?

#ProductMarketing #PMM #GTMStrategy #Positioning #MarketingStrategy

Most on-page SEO "checklists" online are bloated. Here's the 6 that actually move the needle:

𝟭. Title tag includes the primary keyword — naturally, not stuffed 𝟮. First 100 words answer the search intent directly 𝟯. One clear H1, logical H2/H3 structure (not just for looks — search engines parse this) 𝟰. Internal links to 2-3 relevant pages on your own site 𝟱. Meta description written for humans, not bots — it's your ad copy in the SERP 𝟲. Page loads in under 3 seconds on mobile

Everything else (alt text, schema, etc.) matters — but these 6 are where most pages lose the most points.

Save this for your next content audit.

#SEO #ContentMarketing #OnPageSEO

"Backlinks don't matter anymore" is one of the laziest takes in SEO right now.

What's actually true: the quantity game is dead. Buying 500 spammy backlinks does nothing in 2026. But one relevant, high-authority link from a site Google already trusts still moves rankings meaningfully.

The shift isn't "backlinks are dead" — it's "backlink farming is dead." Quality over volume, every time.

If your SEO strategy is still counting links instead of evaluating relevance, you're optimizing for 2015 Google, not today's.

#SEO #DigitalMarketing #ContentStrategy

Apple just quietly upgraded a feature most people forget exists—Maps' "Flyover"—and it’s a masterclass in squeezing more value out of an existing product.  


The problem: Flyover always felt like a bit of a gimmick. It provided cool aerial shots of cities, but it wasn't genuinely useful for planning a trip or exploring a destination you’ve never been to.  


The target user: Travelers scouting a destination before booking, and curious explorers who want a real feel for a city—not just a flat map with pins.  


Why the GTM works: Apple didn't launch a new app or charge extra for this. They upgraded a feature already sitting inside Maps, which nearly every iPhone user already has open weekly.  


- No adoption curve.

- No marketing spend required.

- The distribution was already solved.  


My take: As a marketing student, this resonates with me: sometimes the smartest product move isn't a flashy new launch—it's making an underused feature suddenly worth opening. Retention beats acquisition when the audience is already there.  


Which "boring" feature do you think is quietly getting the biggest glow-up right now? Curious to hear your takes! 👇

#ProductMarketing #GTMStrategy #DigitalMarketing #Apple #GrowthMarketing

Just wrapped up my Microsoft Advertising certifications across Retail, Display, and Search Ads.  


While it's easy to just collect certificates, the real value lies in breaking down the underlying strategy. Here are 3 key takeaways that changed how I think about paid media:  


1. Intent beats reach every single time.
Search ads are uniquely powerful because they meet a user mid-decision. True optimization isn’t just about who you show up for—it’s entirely about when.  


2. Retail media is rapidly eating traditional display.
The boundary between a standard "ad" and an organic "product placement" is disappearing. Modern brands aren’t just bidding for digital eyeballs anymore; they are aggressively competing for virtual shelf space.  


3. Display isn't dead—it’s just frequently misused.
Most display campaigns underperform because they are mistakenly optimized for immediate clicks. In reality, the true strength of display lies in driving frequency and recall—two completely different strategic jobs.  


Certifications are a great foundation, but the real unlock is forcing yourself to critically apply the frameworks rather than just passing the quiz.  


#MicrosoftAdvertising #DigitalMarketing #PPC #PaidMedia #ContinuousLearning
